# 1 Clement Chapter 6 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_006_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 6 extends the martyrdom testimony to anonymous believers, specifically including women. "Danaids and Dirces" (v.2) is one of the most puzzling and evocative phrases in the letter. Two interpretations: (1) The women were executed while costumed as these mythological figures, as Tacitus describes Nero's theatrical executions (Annals 15.44); (2) "Danaids and Dirces" are being used as a figure of speech for "condemned to eternal suffering." Most scholars favor interpretation (1) as it aligns with Tacitus's specific testimony.

The Gen 2:23 citation in v.3 is unexpected: Clement uses marriage's foundation to show how jealousy destroys even the most basic human bond. This is Clement's most personal condemnation — jealousy attacks the family.

---

## Chapter 6

**6:1** To these men who lived in holiness there was joined a great multitude of the elect, who through many indignities and tortures — suffering these things because of jealousy — set among us a most excellent example.

**6:2** Because of jealousy women were persecuted — as Danaids and Dirces — and having endured terrible and unholy outrages, they ran safely the course of faith and received a noble prize, though weak in body.

**6:3** Jealousy has estranged wives from their husbands, and perverted the saying of our father Adam: "This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh." [Gen 2:23 LXX]

**6:4** Jealousy and strife have overthrown great cities and uprooted mighty nations.

---

*SOPHIA consensus translation. Completed 2026-03-17.*
